variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Neuromorphic computing designs algorithms and hardware around local state, asynchronous events, and highly parallel communication inspired by nervous systems. A common implementation uses a spiking neural network (SNN): each neuron keeps a small state, integrates incoming spike events, and emits a new spike only when its state crosses a threshold.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Detect a meaningful change
pairs.detail: An event sensor or encoder emits a timestamped change.
pairs.explanation: An event sensor or encoder emits a timestamped change. The threshold controls a trade-off: too sensitive produces noise traffic; too selective removes task evidence.

pairs.label: Route the event
pairs.detail: The event address and payload travel to connected neuron cores.
pairs.explanation: The event address and payload travel to connected neuron cores. Fan-out, placement, queue depth, and burst rate determine routing pressure.

pairs.label: Update local state
pairs.detail: A neuron updates membrane state from the event, leaks over time, and fires when it crosses a threshold.
pairs.explanation: A neuron updates membrane state from the event, leaks over time, and fires when it crosses a threshold. Synaptic work follows arrived events rather than every possible connection.

pairs.label: Decode a bounded action
pairs.detail: A readout converts spike timing, count, or state into a class, alert, or control output.
pairs.explanation: A readout converts spike timing, count, or state into a class, alert, or control output. The user-visible metric belongs to this complete decision, not to an isolated core.

variants.hint:
Detect a meaningful change: An event sensor or encoder emits a timestamped change.

Route the event: The event address and payload travel to connected neuron cores.

Update local state: A neuron updates membrane state from the event, leaks over time, and fires when it crosses a threshold.

Decode a bounded action: A readout converts spike timing, count, or state into a class, alert, or control output.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Surrogate-gradient training
pairs.detail: Use a smooth proxy derivative during the backward pass while keeping discrete spikes in the forward pass.
pairs.explanation: Use a smooth proxy derivative during the backward pass while keeping discrete spikes in the forward pass. Validate sequence length, threshold dynamics, quantization, and the exact target neuron model.

pairs.label: ANN-to-SNN conversion
pairs.detail: Translate activations into spike rates or timing.
pairs.explanation: Translate activations into spike rates or timing. Conversion can preserve task quality, but long rate windows and dense firing can increase latency and remove event sparsity.

pairs.label: Local plasticity
pairs.detail: STDP or three-factor rules update synapses from local spike traces plus an optional reward signal.
pairs.explanation: STDP or three-factor rules update synapses from local spike traces plus an optional reward signal. Bound updates, monitor activity, and keep a rollbackable base configuration.

pairs.label: Hybrid training and inference
pairs.detail: A dense model may train or resolve ambiguous cases while an event-driven front end handles temporal filtering.
pairs.explanation: A dense model may train or resolve ambiguous cases while an event-driven front end handles temporal filtering. Include every conversion and fallback in the measured boundary.

pairs.detail: Report task quality, calibration, time-to-first-correct decision, and worst-case behavior on identical input traces and decision windows.

pairs.label: Energy evidence

pairs.detail: Slice quiet, typical, burst, noisy, dense, and recovery regimes.
pairs.explanation: Slice quiet, typical, burst, noisy, dense, and recovery regimes. Report queue depth, event loss, state reset, and quality under each stress.
